title: On Task Scope and Information Retention in Source Coding
abstract: arXiv:2609.37575v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We argue that dividing codec design into Coding for Machines (CfM) and Coding for Humans (CfH) is a misleading distinction for deciding what information a codec may discard. Receiver identity does not determine admissible information loss. The required rate depends on task scope, including the predictions to support, their losses and tolerated risks, the encoder observation, and the permitted decoding procedures. Notably, a machine task may have a higher minimum rate than a restricted human decision. Rate savings on selected machine tasks apply only to the stated requirements, not to an intrinsic ordering by receiver type. We extend source and feature coding to finite task families, derive when restricting the encoder observation preserves the minimum rate, and show that equality between source and split-feature coding rates can no longer hold as the task scope expands.

translated_title: 论信源编码中的任务范围与信息保留
translated_abstract: 我们论证了将编解码器设计划分为面向机器的编码（CfM）与面向人类的编码（CfH）这一区分，对于决定编解码器可以丢弃哪些信息而言是一种误导。接收者的身份并不能决定可容许的信息损失。所需的码率取决于任务范围，包括需要支持的预测任务、相应的损失函数与可容忍的风险、编码器的观测量以及允许的解码程序。值得注意的是，一个机器任务的最低码率可能高于一个受限的人类决策任务。在特定机器任务上获得的码率节省仅适用于所声明的需求，而非基于接收者类型的内在排序。我们将信源编码与特征编码扩展到有限任务族，推导出在何种条件下限制编码器观测量能够保持最低码率，并证明随着任务范围的扩大，信源编码与分割特征编码码率之间的相等关系不再成立。
tldr: 该论文提出决定编解码器可丢弃信息的应是任务范围而非接收者类型（面向机器还是面向人类），并将信源编码与特征编码扩展到有限任务族，推导出限制编码器观测保持最低码率的条件，同时证明任务范围扩大时源编码与分割特征编码的码率相等性不再成立。
en_tdlr: The paper argues that task scope—not receiver identity (machine vs. human)—determines what information a codec may discard, and extends source and feature coding to finite task families, showing that the equality between source and split-feature coding rates breaks down as task scope expands.
